chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed the ritual bath for Ihram, then put on a shirt before entering the state of Ihram. He said: 'His bath has been invalidated.'

key_terms.الْإِحْرَامُ: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: Does putting on clothes before entering Ihram invalidate the ritual bath?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the juristic principle that the ritual bath for Ihram is intrinsically linked to the immediate act of entering the state of consecration. Al-Shaykh al-Tusi records this view, indicating that premature dressing breaks the continuity of the ritual act, thereby nullifying the ghusl and requiring its repetition. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the precise timing and intentionality required in the transition from purity to the sacred state of Ihram.
